ticket: JSRT-19 NamedEvaluation (cross-directory) + remaining annexB clusters (B.3.4 if-position, B.3.3.1 parameter exception, __proto__ isProtoSetter exclusion)

items.root_cause: Confirmed via direct probe (end of JSRT-18) that IsAnonymousFunctionDefinition/SetFunctionName is not implemented for ANY binding form: `let fn = function(){}; fn.name` already yields '' with no using/await-using involved. Affects var/let/const initializers, destructuring defaults, object-literal properties (incl. computed keys), class fields (public/private, instance/static), export default (desugars to a plain `const \0module.default = expr;`), and simple assignment/logical-assignment where the value is a genuinely anonymous function/arrow/class source expression (not merely a nameless value produced some other way).
items.fix: Ported/adapted from lucid-softworks/lumen (crates/lumen/src/eval.rs) @ f6c9860d44fa52249cfd647122edea184d32c863, MIT. Added `is_anonymous_function_definition` (spec 8.6.2: transparent through CoverParenthesizedExpression/`ExprKind::Paren`, true for a nameless Function/Arrow/Class expression, false otherwise -- confirmed against Test262's actual fn-name-cover.js content that `(function(){})` is anonymous-eligible but `(0, function(){})` (a Sequence under the parens) is not) and `property_key_as_fn_name` (spec 7.3.9: string key as-is, symbol key as `[description]`/`''`) to interp_helpers.rs. Added a new `named_evaluation(&self, source: &ast::Expr, value: &mut JsValue, name: &str)` to interp_stmt.rs (checks `is_anonymous_function_definition(source)` before naming) as a SEPARATE method from the pre-existing `infer_function_name` (2-arg, unconditional, value-based) -- `infer_function_name`'s signature and behavior are kept exactly as-is because `crates/amazing-js/src/vm/mod.rs` (js-vm-owned, a real separate Rust module outside the flat include! chain) independently calls it with the old 2-arg form for its own bytecode assignment path, and `assignment_preserves_legacy_function_name_inference` differentially checks both backends agree; changing that signature or its unconditional semantics would have broken vm/mod.rs's build or that cross-backend parity test. `named_evaluation` call sites added: StmtKind::Var's initializer (with a `\0module.default` -> `"default"` name-mapping for export-default, since module.rs already desugars both `export default expr;` and an anonymous `export default function/class` into that one Var form -- no module.rs edit needed); `Binding::Default`'s declaration-side destructuring default (interp_helpers.rs's `bind_pattern_mode`); `bind_params`'s simple parameter default; `assign_pattern_expr`'s `ExprKind::Assign{op:Assign,..}` (assignment-pattern-side destructuring default) and `PropValue::CoverInitializedName`; the object-literal `PropValue::Init` property arm (via `property_key_as_fn_name`, with an explicit isProtoSetter exclusion -- see the __proto__ fix below); `define_field` in interp_class_private.rs (public and private fields, keyed by the field's already-resolved `FieldKey` per ClassFieldDefinitionEvaluation's ordering, instance and static). Plain `=`/`&&=`/`||=`/`??=` assignment expressions deliberately keep the OLD unconditional `infer_function_name` heuristic (no `is_anonymous_function_definition` check) rather than switching to precise NamedEvaluation, to preserve exact parity with vm/mod.rs's own independent heuristic and the differential test that checks it -- an initial attempt to restrict this call to `Reference::Binding` targets only (still without the precise check) regressed every top-level `name = () => {}` assignment (`language/expressions/assignment/fn-name-*.js`), because `resolve_reference` resolves a global-scope target to `Reference::Property` (via `global_binding_object`), not `Reference::Binding` -- fixed by using `reference_name(&reference)` (matching vm/mod.rs's own exact pattern: `if let Some(name) = reference_name(&reference) { infer_function_name(...) }`) instead of restricting by `Reference` variant.
items.target_tests: language/expressions, language/statements, built-ins/Function (the fn-name-* cluster everywhere)

items.item: Annex B.3.4: bare, brace-less if-position FunctionDeclaration (`if (x) function f(){} [else function g(){}]`)
items.root_cause: Explicit known gap carried over from JSRT-18's evidence, confirmed as the single largest remaining annexB cluster (~200+ of the 475 remaining failures: 'outer/inner declaration' mismatches, 'f is not defined', 'identifier already declared', missing ReferenceErrors, 'binding value updated following evaluation'). The existing Annex B.3.3 sync (StmtKind::Function's exec_stmt arm) only fires correctly when a StmtKind::Block's block-entry pre-pass already created a per-occurrence local lexical binding to read from (`env.local_cell`); a bare if/else branch is never wrapped in a Block at all, so there is no such binding. A first attempt made the generic StmtKind::Function arm itself synthesize a fallback implicit block whenever `env.local_cell` returned None -- this compiled and passed the crate suite, but a targeted probe (`if (false) function _f(){} else function f(){return "inner";} function f(){return "outer";}`) showed it still returned "outer", not "inner": `env.local_cell` found the UNRELATED ordinary top-level `f` declaration's own pre-existing var-scope cell (created by hoist_inner's eager top-level bind, since the two `f`s share a name) and treated it as if it were this if-branch's own binding, reading and re-syncing THAT stale value back instead of ever creating the if-branch's own closure.
items.fix: Adapted from lucid-softworks/lumen (crates/lumen/src/eval.rs, annexb_fn_sync_eval) @ f6c9860d, MIT. Moved the B.3.4 handling out of the generic StmtKind::Function arm entirely and into a new `exec_if_branch` helper, called from StmtKind::If's own exec_stmt arm instead of a bare `self.exec_stmt(branch, env)`: when the chosen branch is itself `StmtKind::Function` (sloppy mode, non-async, non-generator) it ALWAYS creates a fresh implicit one-name Block (`EnvHandle::new(EnvKind::Block, ...)`), builds the closure there via `make_function`, lexically binds it, and syncs that value out to `env.var_scope()` -- never falling back to reading whatever `env.local_cell` happens to already hold under that name. The generic StmtKind::Function arm reverted to its exact JSRT-18 shape (B.3.3 Block-pre-pass sync only; no fallback creation), since it is documented to assume `env` IS the specific Block that pre-bound this exact occurrence, which is never true for a bare if/else branch. Every other bare-statement position (while/for/labeled/...) does not grammatically permit a FunctionDeclaration at all, so the special case is scoped to If alone.

items.item: Annex B.3.3.1: parameter-name exception for the B.3.4 fix above
items.root_cause: The B.3.4 fix above initially regressed 10 previously-passing annexB/language/function-code/if-decl-*-func-skip-{param,dft-param}.js tests, all testing spec text: 'the extension is NOT observed when there is a formal parameter with the same name' (B.3.3.1: skip the whole extension, not merely a no-op sync, when F is a BoundName of the enclosing function's own parameter list). `scope.local_cell(name).is_some_and(|c| !c.is_lexical())` cannot distinguish a genuine hoist_inner Annex-B var placeholder from a pre-existing, same-scope, same-name formal parameter cell -- `EnvHandle::hoist_var` already leaves an existing binding (parameter or otherwise) untouched, so both look identical at that check.
items.fix: Added `current_function_param_names(&self) -> Vec<String>` (reads `self.frames.last().own_function`'s `JsObject.func.params` and flattens each `ast::Param`'s binding via the pre-existing `binding_names` helper, covering destructuring parameters too). `exec_if_branch` now skips the whole B.3.4 sync (leaving the parameter's own value untouched, matching the 'skip' tests' expectation) when the if-branch's function name collides with a current-frame parameter name, before doing the `scope.local_cell`/is_lexical check at all.

items.root_cause: The new object-literal PropValue::Init NamedEvaluation call (added for the main NamedEvaluation item above) fired unconditionally for every property key, including a non-computed `__proto__:` key -- but PropertyDefinitionEvaluation (spec 13.2.5.5) explicitly sets `isProtoSetter = true` for that exact shape and skips NamedEvaluation entirely (the value becomes the object's [[Prototype]], never an own property, and must NOT be named "__proto__"). Regressed language/expressions/object/__proto__-fn-name.js (before=pass, after=fail) in the very same before/after gate as the B.3.4 work.
items.fix: Added the same non-computed-`__proto__`-key check the object literal's existing [[Prototype]]-assignment special case already uses (`!matches!(&p.key, PropKey::Computed(_)) && k.as_string() == Some("__proto__")`) as a guard directly around the new `named_evaluation` call in the `PropValue::Init` arm, so the anonymous-function value keeps its original (usually empty) name.

known_gaps: Annex B promotion out of try/catch/finally block bodies is still unimplemented (unchanged from JSRT-18 -- hoist_inner's Try arm deliberately still starts a fresh, non-nested hoist).

Annex B's legacy RegExp static accessors/methods (RegExp.$1-$9, input, lastMatch, lastParen, leftContext, rightContext, RegExp.prototype.compile, and a Symbol.split/toint32-limit-recompiles-source detail) do not exist at all -- confirmed via sampling as a second, sizable, wholly separate unimplemented feature cluster (contributes to the 'value is not callable' and 'Expected SameValue(undefined,function)' buckets in the remaining annexB failures). Not attempted this ticket: it is a real new builtin surface, not a hoisting/naming fix, and the ticket's explicit 'cluster them and port them in bulk' scope was spent on the two hoisting/naming clusters above, which were larger and directly tractable from the existing interpreter model.

StmtKind::Switch has no Annex B hoisting arm in hoist_inner at all, and switch statements do not create their own lexical block environment in exec_stmt either -- a plausible explanation for remaining func-switch-case-*/func-switch-dflt-* failures, sampled but not fixed this ticket (time budget spent on the larger if-position and parameter-exception clusters instead).

GeneratorFunction/AsyncGeneratorFunction and async-function/async-generator-body disposal gaps are unchanged from JSRT-17/18 (still js-vm-blocked); see js-runtime_jsrt17_evidence.json and js-runtime_jsrt18_evidence.json.
